name: Record Operations: Separate Model, Contract and Execution Evidence
description: Opt-in, fixed record operations with local arithmetic proof, independent Lean model audit, finite implementation checks and detected host variants.
result_message: Result: Local contract, independent model and finite checks passed; Python correspondence and production safety remain unproved.

intro: Step 1: Check a local version contract and its deliberately broken implementation.
Step 2: Exercise fixed data proposals and detect broken execution paths.
Step 3: Audit the independent Lean model without promoting Python behavior.
narrative.before: A local arithmetic proof cannot establish current authority or prevent a host from bypassing the executor.
narrative.after: Separate evidence shows what was proved in the model and what was observed in the fixed implementation.

harness_contract.intent: Keep model proofs, local contracts and finite record-operation observations distinct.
artifact_contracts: Demo .mm and Python execution inputs are copied to the report directory; proposal JSON cannot choose variants or alter reference cases, principal, store or policy.
No LLM, credentials, external database or certificate promotion is used.
The model is rebuilt and audited without optional skips; selected source identities and kernel logs are retained.

intent_fidelity.source_intent: Current authority and state must govern fixed record updates, with honest evidence boundaries.
success_criteria: Authorized read/update succeeds and denials preserve records.
Four named host variants fail their intended reference cases.
Local version arithmetic verifies while a fixed incorrect body is rejected.
Independent model theorems pass the kernel axiom audit without claiming Python correspondence.
intent_fidelity.drift_risk: Source hashes bind local snapshots only; the trusted host and model/implementation correspondence remain explicit boundaries.

declared_assumptions: The host chooses a truthful, current principal and owns initial state, policy and all code; there is no real authentication.
The fixed role policy and reference cases express the intended demo requirements; policy quality is not proved.
Python, Z3, Lean, the kernel axiom allowlist, build scripts and the evidence collector are trusted.
unverified_connections: The independent Lean model is not proved semantically equivalent to Python parsing, locking, mutation, policy management or failure handling.
The .mm contract proves only local version arithmetic; it is not a proof of the executor, authorization or the Lean/Python connection.
Local source/report hashes establish snapshot consistency, not authenticity, deployed artifact identity or safe execution.
out_of_scope: Real authentication, production storage, HTTP, external delivery, cross-process/distributed transactions and deployment safety.
Arbitrary host-code confinement, privileged direct writes, dynamic delegation/revocation and persistent audit delivery.
The l2_agent layer runs only finite Python fixtures, not an LLM, mumei-agent repair or formal test-to-contract translation.
